title: [YouPass Collect] - Percentage of food and goods bought from supermarkets

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar charts illustrate the proportions of food and goods purchased from supermarkets in three European countries in 1998 and 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the percentages of both food and goods bought from supermarkets increased in most countries over the period shown. Country A experienced the most significant growth in both categories, while Country C maintained the lowest figures throughout the decade.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding food purchases from supermarkets, Country B led in 1998 with approximately 22% of food being bought from these establishments, which was about twice the figure for Country A and four times that of Country C, at around 10% and 5% respectively. By 2008, however, Country A had overtaken Country B, with its percentage rising dramatically to 35%, while Country B saw a modest increase to 27%. Meanwhile, Country C's figure doubled to approximately 10% by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for goods bought from supermarkets, the pattern was somewhat similar. Country B again recorded the highest percentage in 1998, at roughly 23%, while Country A's figure stood at just 5%, and no data was available for Country C. Over the following decade, Country A witnessed a substantial surge to about 40%, surpassing Country B's figure of 25%. Country C reported approximately 15% of goods being purchased from supermarkets in 2008.
